title: ProjectE topology change proposals
description: Output of tools/scripts/topology_advise.py. Every other solver in this bundle optimises WITHIN a fixed topology; this proposes changing it. What comes out are hypotheses, not fixes: each names what it adds, which way a metric moves, the tool that would verify it, the observation that would refute it, and its cost. 'runs_no_solver' and 'measures_nothing' are both pinned true - a magnitude in this report would be read as a result.

status.description: RED only when an input or the catalogue itself failed to load. The tool measures nothing, so it cannot find a defect in a design; a shortfall it cannot address is NO_COVERAGE.

measures_nothing.description: Triggered by shortfalls other tools measured. Measuring here would give the repo two answers to one question, which is the #51 and #54 failure.

runs_no_solver.description: Directions come from topological arguments. Magnitudes come from the named verifier and appear in ITS report, never here.

context.description: Facts supplied by the caller that rule transformations out. Never inferred: whether a reference plane is split is something reference_plane.py measures.

observations.description: Only FAIL and NO_COVERAGE findings become observations. A PASS is not a shortfall, and proposing against one is how a tool starts recommending work for its own sake.

issue.description: An excluded proposal is an ANSWER, not a violation - often the most informative line in the report.

magnitude.description: Always null, and required to be present so the absence is explicit rather than an omission a reader might fill in. The verifier named in verify_with produces the quantity.

cost.description: Required on every offered proposal. One listing only benefits is a sales pitch.

uncovered.description: Shortfalls the catalogue has nothing to say about. Listed rather than omitted: a proposal list that silently drops what it could not address looks like complete coverage of the report it read.
